To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the two-stage sampling systems (i), (ii), and (iii) are superior to the system (iv) in terms of the variance of the estimator of the total of a variable in each of the strata.

the use of stratified two-stage samples with probability proportional to a measure of size for the first stage selection and without replacement for the second stage selection, results in a substantial reduction in the variance of the estimate of the total, as compared to the use of stratification, simple random samples and without replacement.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a sampling system which will provide the best possible estimate of the total of a certain agricultural item in North Carolina, subject to the constraint that the total cost of sampling must not exceed a certain specified amount.
the development of a theory of sampling systems which will provide the best estimates of totals with the least possible cost.
the development of methods of sampling and estimation of agricultural statistics which have a high degree of accuracy at a minimum cost.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the system of selecting two primary sampling units from one stratum, one with probability proportional to the size of the unit and the other with probability 1/2, is the most economical of the systems investigated.

the system of sampling without replacement, with one of the two primary sampling units selected with probability proportional, to some measure of the size and the other unit selected with equal probability, is the best of the three sampling systems investigated.
the sampling systems which use the stratified two-stage method of selection and estimation are more efficient than the sampling systems which employ only the stratified single-stage method.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the system (i) is superior to the others in terms of efficiency and that the system (ii) should not be used.

the stratified sampling systems with two-stage sampling are more efficient than the single-stage sampling systems, and the stratified systems with selection of two primary units without replacement are more efficient than those with selection of two units with probability proportional to their size.

the system which uses two primary units, with one unit selected with probability proportional size and the other selected with equal probability, appears to be the best of the three sampling systems investigated.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of the stratified two-stage system with the selection of two units without replacement is more efficient than either the stratified two stage system with replacement or the stratified simple random sampling system.

the two-stage sampling systems with replacement are less efficient than the systems without replacement, and that the two-stage system with replacement and probability proportional to size for both primary sampling units is less efficient than the system with equal probability of selection for the second primary unit.
we have developed a new method for estimating the number of primary sampling systems.
